newsitem.title: UK: UK to promote EU cooperation at IGC and beyond.
newsitem.headline: UK to promote EU cooperation at IGC and beyond.

text.p: The new Labour government said on Wednesday it would use next month's European Union summit and Britain's presidency of the EU in the first half of next year to increase cooperation while promoting British interests.

Queen Elizabeth, in a speech delivered to open the new session of parliament, said: "They will pursue an outcome to the Intergovernmental Conference and use their Presidency in the first half of 1998 to strengthen European cooperation while advancing the United Kingdom's interests and which makes the Union more open, democratic and efficient."
The speech was written for The Queen by cabinet ministers and was accompanied by an explanatory government note which laid out Britain's priorities at the IGC. They included --
-- adapting the decision-making machinery in preparation for enlargement and to improve democracy
-- signing up to the Social Chapter, a new Employment Chapter, Treaty provisions on human rights and non-discrimination, fighting fraud
-- an effective, intergovernmental common foreign and security policy
-- clear recognition of the UK's right to maintain frontier controls
-- a solution to quota-hopping by foreign fishing crews
The IGC summit will take place in Amsterdam in mid-June.
